### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **54** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**51** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2ae3e30154261888162062cdf19563fa160d6ca6`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `environmentId (43 routes)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **14** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2ae3e30154261888162062cdf19563fa160d6ca6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `91a2099457504111eead71c5038c4bae8e40559e` — the merge of head `6a9ae1bd4cbb7540ed032497d525e721e20855ce` into base `2ae3e30154261888162062cdf19563fa160d6ca6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 91a2099457504111eead71c5038c4bae8e40559e && git checkout 91a2099457504111eead71c5038c4bae8e40559e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2ae3e30154261888162062cdf19563fa160d6ca6 6a9ae1bd4cbb7540ed032497d525e721e20855ce && git checkout -B drift-repro 2ae3e30154261888162062cdf19563fa160d6ca6 && git merge --no-ff 6a9ae1bd4cbb7540ed032497d525e721e20855ce

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2ae3e30154261888162062cdf19563fa160d6ca6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2ae3e30154261888162062cdf19563fa160d6ca6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `359ed69a99c5d23dc0d7c0377d136cf660c71812`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #30964 (body and all seven comments, including triage 6687756412, the cloud-half input 6696363641, the claim 6717251809, the amendments 6719677711 and 6719701725, and the dev report 6720213406), the PR #31475 body, its 35-file list, the net diff `origin/main...359ed69a` (842 insertions, 30 deletions), and the check-runs on this head. The ruling quoted on the card is cloud#3624 ruling A, 「A + 两边审计 + 转发安装人（推荐）」.

Check-runs on this head, all completed by 2026-11-08T10:36Z: 58 runs, of which 36 succeeded, 20 were skipped, 2 were cancelled, and none failed. The two cancelled runs (`Auto Label`, `Check Changeset`) are duplicate triggers; each has a sibling run of the same name that succeeded (`Check Changeset` twice). Every derived gate family that ran is green, including Test Core 1-8 of 8, all four Type Check jobs, every Lint job (among them `scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, which was red before the fix in `359ed69a`), `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`POST /api/v1/cloud-connection/install` accepts `install_mode` or `installMode`. Right.** `installModeOf` (`packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts:284`) parses the value against `InstallModeSchema` by reference. It refuses a value outside the enum, or two spellings that disagree, with 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` before any control-plane call. Strictly, a body such as `{ package_id, install_mode: 'copy' }` used to install managed and now gets 400. I do not count that as a narrowing of a published accept set. The route never declared the key: its own header comment documents `{ package_id, seed_sample_data? }`, and the route ledger records it as server-only, with no `@objectstack/client` method. Its only in-repo sender is the Console (pending changeset `30963-hosted-install-mode.md`), which sends only enum values. Refusing an unreadable mode instead of silently installing managed matches what install-local does with its own `installMode`.
2. **The control-plane request gains `install_mode` and `installer_user_id`. Right, and it matches 6696363641.** `install_mode` is snake_case and sent only when the caller named a mode, so absent still means managed (`cloud-connection-plugin.ts:1029`). `installer_user_id` is a body param on the same `sys_package.install_package` action, never a header. Its value is `session.userId` from the session this door admitted (`:1040`), never a body value. The test at `cloud-connection-plugin.test.ts` sends `installer_user_id` and `installerUserId` in the body and pins that neither reaches the control plane. Triage's question (how the control plane bounds the asserted user) is answered in the PR body by citing 6696363641, and this PR leaves that bound unchanged.
3. **The answer on an unmanaged grant is the install-local door's answer, with a new 502 and 503. Right, with S1.** A control-plane refusal and every managed answer are relayed exactly as before (`:1046`). A grant that does not echo `install_mode: 'unmanaged'`, or that has no `version_id`, answers 502 `PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED`, copies nothing, and never reads `data.manifest` (`:1078`). A missing door answers 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. Both are pinned by tests: five unreadable grants, and the missing-door case. The 502 code and status are the ones this route already used for a thrown install. The changeset bullets name the 400, 502 and 503 answers. The Clause-② line names the door's answer.
4. **The new in-process service `marketplace-install-local` (`install-local-door-service.ts`, registered in `MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin.init` and declared in `providesServices`). Right, and it bypasses no gate.** `install(request)` calls the same `handleInstall` that `POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local` mounts. It goes through `routeContextOf`, which I checked against every `c.req.*` member the handler and `readJsonRequestBody` read: `json`, `text`, `header`, `raw`, `param`, `params`, `query`, plus `c.json`. The first thing `handleInstall` does is `requireInstallCapability`. That resolves the principal from `c.req.raw.headers` through `resolveAuthzContext`, applies the held-session gate, and then requires `install_local`. The cloud-connection door passes the caller's own headers, adds no `Authorization`, and sends the body `{ packageId, versionId, installMode: 'unmanaged' }` plus `seedSampleData` only when the caller asked for it. So the copy runs as the installing user, through the same protocol handshake, namespace check, `installUnmanaged` copy record and installer-owned sample rows. The service admits only what the forwarded credentials authenticate, so it does not widen who may install. `INSTALL_LOCAL_DOOR_SERVICE` is not exported from the package index, so only the service name is public.
5. **`sys_audit_log.action` gains `package_unmanaged_import`. Right.** This is option A as ruled in 6719701725: a new action, not a reused `import` with a `metadata.kind`. The option is added writer-first (`sys-audit-log.object.ts:438`). The labels test, the writer inventory and the deployment-level-rows integration test each name it.
6. **The audit row goes through plugin-audit's writer and is not hand-built. Right.** `installUnmanaged` hands the `audit` slot's `recordPackageLifecycleEvent` one event on the failure path (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:4844`) and one on the success path (`:4866`). The event type is declared structurally in cloud-connection, as metadata-protocol does for the uninstall event, so there is no package dependency on plugin-audit. `buildPackageLifecycleAuditRow` (`package-lifecycle-audit.ts:211`) builds the row: deployment-level (`tenant_id`, `object_name` and `record_id` null), with `metadata` holding source, version, new base, namespace, `copied_count` and `outcome`, and on failure `error_code` and `status` but never the message. That covers every field Ask 4 lists. The success event is written only after the import has returned, and that path always answers 200, so the row cannot say `success` for an answer that failed. A throwing slot is logged at `error` and changes no answer, and a test pins this.
7. **plugin-audit's exported types change shape. Not a published narrowing, but undeclared (S2).** `PackageLifecycleAuditEvent` becomes the union `PackageUninstallAuditEvent | PackageUnmanagedImportAuditEvent` (`package-lifecycle-audit.ts:110`). `PackageLifecycleAuditAction` widens. `PACKAGE_UNMANAGED_IMPORT_AUDIT_ACTION`, `PackageUninstallAuditEvent` and `PackageUnmanagedImportAuditEvent` are new exports (`index.ts:51-57`). A reader who took `itemsFailed` off the old interface would now have to narrow on `action`. That interface has never been published, though: it arrived with #31186, whose changeset `31186-package-uninstall-audit-row.md` is still pending and is absent from `CHANGELOG.md` (last entry 18.3.0). So no published shape is narrowed. Neither the Clause-② line nor the changeset names these exports.
8. **The regenerated translation files carry only the new label. Right.** Each of the 11 `*.objects.generated.ts` files adds only `package_unmanaged_import: "Package Unmanaged Import"`, plus the comma on the line before it. Each of the 10 non-English `*.source-hashes.generated.ts` files adds only the one hash `676d7ce8c9d1fda4`, in sorted position. `en` has no hash file on main. No other key moved. `git diff pr31475 origin/main` over the translations directory shows no drift beyond those lines, so `ru` (#30512) is already covered.
9. **Nothing under `packages/spec` or `docs/adr` changed.** The net diff over `packages/spec` and `docs` is 0 lines. `InstallModeSchema` is read, not changed.
10. **The PR body describes the code accurately, with two exceptions.** Everything I checked matches the code: the tests it lists (3 forwarding cases, 8 unmanaged-grant cases, 4 install-modes cases, 2 row cases), the fail-closed shapes, the header handling, and the acceptance note that a caller without `install_local` gets 403 after the control plane recorded its grant and leaves no environment row. The two exceptions are S3, a cross-repo fact stated as true, and N1, a code comment that is no longer true.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset is `.changeset/30964-unmanaged-grant-copy-and-audit.md`, `patch` on `@objectstack/cloud-connection` and `@objectstack/plugin-audit`. These are the two released packages the diff moves. With `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch` is the level AGENTS.md (Post-Task §3) requires.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right, and the PR body and changeset carry the same line. The diff widens a route's accept set, an outbound request, an answer, a service name, a select value and the event a writer accepts. It narrows nothing published (see ①1 and ①7). It is not breaking, so no ADR-0087 marker and no migration are owed.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. `sys_audit_log.action` is a readonly ledger field written by the platform, not something a metadata author writes. `install_mode` reuses the existing `InstallModeSchema` without changing it, and no spec key changed.
- The Clause-② line omits the plugin-audit export changes in ①7. See S2.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`: none.** The dev report lists `[]`.
- **Dev flag: `target_namespace` is held back (carrier: seat).** I accept this. The amendment 6719677711 rules it ("held back until cloud says it reads it"), and the PR body states it under the cross-repo NOT MEASURED heading. The follow-up card is owed by the seat and is not yet filed. That is the seat's chore, not a defect in this PR.
- **Dev flag: the copy needs `install_local` while the door admits any signed-in session (carrier: none). Escalated as S4.** A grant that the install-local door then refuses before the import runs leaves the control plane's grant row with no environment row. That holds for a capability 403, a handshake refusal, a manifest fetch failure or the walled-catalog refusal. Ruling A's 「两边审计」 and Ask 4 ("success or failure … only the environment knows") leave that half unpaired. The PR states this gap honestly in its acceptance notes. It needs a carrier, not `none`.
- **`security_findings`: none. I agree.** The installer is the admitted session's id, never request input. The control plane's membership bound is the cloud half's, and it is cited, not changed.
- **Cross-repo facts.** The grant's shape is stated as NOT MEASURED and fails closed: 502 and nothing copied, pinned by five cases. `target_namespace` is stated as NOT MEASURED. Whether a hosted environment kernel mounts `MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin` is cross-repo, but it is stated as fact. It fails closed (503), but it is not declared NOT MEASURED (S3).

### Findings

- **S1. The 502 for an unread grant can misreport what the control plane did** (`packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts:1078-1091`). A control plane older than cloud#3683 ignores `install_mode` and installs the package managed, and its answer then echoes no mode. This door answers 502 "Nothing was copied". That sentence is literally true, but the package did land managed. Before this PR, the Console read that same answer as "the environment installed the package managed instead" (`30963-hosted-install-mode.md`). Now the user sees a failure while a managed install exists, and is likely to retry.
  - Fix: when `data.install_mode` is absent, say so in the 502 message and the warn line, for example "The control plane did not echo `install_mode`; a control plane that does not read it may have installed the package managed. Check Installed before retrying." Alternatively, relay that one answer unchanged so the Console's existing managed-fallback text applies. In either case, keep the 502 for an echo of `unmanaged` with no `version_id` and for an echo of a different mode, and extend the fail-closed test to pin the new text for the absent-echo case.
- **S2. The changeset and the Clause-② line omit plugin-audit's export changes** (`.changeset/30964-unmanaged-grant-copy-and-audit.md:8,16`; `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts:51-57`; `package-lifecycle-audit.ts:105-110`).
  - Fix: in the changeset's audit bullet, add one sentence: "`@objectstack/plugin-audit` exports `PACKAGE_UNMANAGED_IMPORT_AUDIT_ACTION`, `PackageUninstallAuditEvent` and `PackageUnmanagedImportAuditEvent`; `PackageLifecycleAuditEvent` is now their union (narrow on `action`), and `PackageLifecycleAuditAction` gains `package_unmanaged_import`."
  - Add a matching clause to the Clause-② line in the PR body and the changeset, for example "; plugin-audit exports the event types and the action constant".
- **S3. A cross-repo deployment fact is stated as true** (`packages/cloud-connection/src/install-local-door-service.ts:29-31` "where its plugin runs"; the PR body bullet "In a multi-tenant deployment the door is read from the environment's own kernel (`kernel-manager`), where the install-local plugin runs"). `kernel-manager` and the hosted environment kernel's plugin list are composed in objectstack-ai/cloud and cannot be read here. This repo's own text says the opposite of the claim on main: `30963-hosted-install-mode.md:10` reads "On a hosted environment (a cloud base, no install-local door)", and `MarketplacePage.tsx:581-590` reads the same. If the hosted environment kernel does not mount the plugin, every unmanaged grant answers 503 after the control plane has recorded it. The code fails closed, so this is a gap in the prose.
  - Fix: move the claim under "Cross-repo, NOT MEASURED" in the PR body: "the hosted environment kernel is assumed to mount `MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin`; if it does not, every unmanaged grant answers 503 and nothing is copied". Reword the docblock line as that same assumption.
  - The seat should also file a cloud-side follow-up so the hosted environment kernel mounts the plugin, or confirms that it already does.
- **S4. A grant refused before the import leaves no environment audit row, and the gap has no carrier** (dev report 6720213406 `out_of_scope_findings[1]`; `packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts:1047`).
  - Fix: the seat files a follow-up card. The PR's Acceptance notes then link that card instead of "not filed".
  - The follow-up would have `copyOnUnmanagedGrant`, or `handleInstall` when `installMode === 'unmanaged'`, hand the writer one `package_unmanaged_import` failure event with the door's code and status for every refusal after the grant.
- **N1. Two code comments are out of date** (`packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts:1005-1008`, `:974`).
  - Fix: at `:1008`, replace "so a managed install's request is the one it always was" with "so a managed install's request differs from before only by `installer_user_id`". It is now always sent, as the PR body itself says.
  - At `:974`, change the route header from `{ package_id, seed_sample_data? }` to `{ package_id, seed_sample_data?, install_mode? }`.
- **N2. The in-process door test promises "same gates" but exercises only the malformed-JSON refusal** (`packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-install-modes.test.ts:1198`).
  - Fix: add one call through `h.door.install` with headers for a principal without `install_local`, and expect 403 `FORBIDDEN`, no `importUnmanagedPackage` call and no audit event. That pins the "no bypass" property directly instead of relying on `handleInstall` being the same function.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-b11gkm`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5pXkgNXVpCn2GZDjyy`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `6a9ae1bd4cbb7540ed032497d525e721e20855ce`
Local-runs: none

This is the delta review of 6720446134, which passed `359ed69a` with findings S1–S4, N1 and N2. It judges only `git diff 359ed69a..6a9ae1bd` (one commit, 5 files, 80 insertions, 10 deletions), the changeset, and the PR body as it stands at 2026-11-08T11:20Z ("seat refresh (round 1)"). The two follow-up issues the delta links, #31481 and #31482, were read too. Everything else in 6720446134 stands as written, with one correction in ①4 below.

Check-runs on this head, read at 11:22Z: 49 runs. 14 succeeded, 15 were skipped, none failed, and 20 are still in progress. The 20 running are Test Core 1–8 of 8, Build Core, Live E2E UI, all four Type Check jobs, and six Lint jobs (`ESLint`, `docs & code guards`, `repo & tooling gates`, `CI, release & engine gates`, `scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `scoped · query-options erasure`). These are NOT MEASURED: no conclusion exists, so no test, type or lint verdict on this head is claimed here. The ones that succeeded include both `PR-body guards` runs, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests` and `Dogfood Regression Gate`.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **S1, fixed.** The 502 for an unread grant now names the possible managed install (`packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts:1080-1104`).
   - `unechoed` is true only when `data?.install_mode` is `undefined` or `null`, so an answer with no `data` at all also counts. In that case the 502 message and the warn line both end with "The control plane did not echo install_mode; a control plane that does not read it may have installed the package managed. Check Installed before retrying."
   - An echoed `managed`, an echoed `unmanaged` with no `version_id`, and an echoed `unmanaged` with a blank `version_id` keep the plain 502. The code and status are unchanged (`PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED`, 502), and nothing is copied.
   - The new test (`cloud-connection-plugin.test.ts:491-514`) pins both halves on both the message and the warn line. Its inputs are `{ version_id }`, `{ install_mode: null, version_id }` and `{}` on one side, and `managed`, missing `version_id` and blank `version_id` on the other. Each `grant()` call builds a fresh `ctx`, so the warn-line assertions cannot leak between iterations. The earlier fail-closed test uses `toContain('Nothing was copied')`, so the appended sentence does not break it.
   - The only change to a published shape is the text of an existing error message. The body, the changeset and the Chinese summary (item 3) describe the code accurately.
2. **S2, fixed.** The changeset's Clause-② line, its new "New plugin-audit exports" bullet, and the PR body's Clause-② line now name `PACKAGE_UNMANAGED_IMPORT_AUDIT_ACTION`, `PackageUninstallAuditEvent` and `PackageUnmanagedImportAuditEvent`. They also state that `PackageLifecycleAuditEvent` is now their union (narrow it on `action`) and that `PackageLifecycleAuditAction` gains `package_unmanaged_import`. This matches `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts:47-60` and `package-lifecycle-audit.ts:98,105,110` on this head. The delta does not touch `packages/plugins`. The two Clause-② lines differ slightly in wording (the body ends "No spec schema changes"), but they say the same thing. `PR-body guards` and `Check Changeset` succeeded.
3. **S3, fixed.** The hosted-kernel mount is now stated as an assumption in three places, and each one links #31482:
   - The `install-local-door-service.ts:31-37` docblock now reads "Cross-repo, NOT MEASURED: that a hosted environment's kernel mounts the install-local plugin at all". It cites the 30963 changeset and `MarketplacePage` as contrary evidence. The "where its plugin runs" assertion is gone.
   - The changeset's cross-repo bullet carries the same assumption.
   - The PR body's "Cross-repo, NOT MEASURED" section and its multi-tenant bullet carry it too.
   - Each says the failure answer is 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. That matches the code: the 503 message names `MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin is not mounted` (`cloud-connection-plugin.ts:1117-1124`).
   - #31482 is open and covers the mount question and fixing the 30963 prose.
4. **N2, fixed. Correction to 6720446134: the door requires `manage_metadata`, not `install_local`.** The developer is right that the capability is `manage_metadata`.
   - `requireInstallCapability` (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:7146-7172`) refuses with 403 `FORBIDDEN` "… requires the `manage_metadata` capability", because `INSTALL_LOCAL_CAPABILITY = 'manage_metadata'` (`:543`, ADR-0066 D1's authoring key, not an install-specific capability).
   - Round 1 misnamed this key `install_local` in ①4, ①10, the ③ dev flag and N2. Every one of those judgments holds with the right name.
   - The PR body now names `(manage_metadata)` in three places: the gate list, the Tests list and the Acceptance note. The changeset names no key ("the installer's install capability"). Both are consistent with the code.
   - The new test (`marketplace-install-local-install-modes.test.ts:1230-1245`) calls `h.door.install` with an installer that holds no permission set. `grantless` wraps `withInstallerGrants`, a plain object, so overriding `find` takes effect and cannot recurse. The test expects 403 `FORBIDDEN`, a message containing "requires the `manage_metadata` capability", no `importUnmanagedPackage` call, and `auditEvents` empty. The message check proves the 403 comes from the capability gate, not from authentication or the held-session check. That pins the "no bypass" property N2 asked for.
5. **N1, half fixed; one nit remains (N1′ below).** The route header now reads `{ package_id, seed_sample_data?, install_mode? }` (`:974`). A new comment at `:1016-1017` says the installer is "always sent" as `installer_user_id`. But the comment at `:1003-1007` still ends "so a managed install's request is the one it always was". That is still false, and the PR body itself says the request "differs from today's only by the installer".
6. **Nothing else in the delta is false, and nothing widens or narrows a published shape.** The delta changes no route, no outbound request, no service, no select value and no export. Its only runtime change is the appended sentence in ①1. Two body claims check out against the history: the Tests counts (9 unmanaged-grant cases, 5 install-modes cases) match the files, and `c0dc4059` is an ancestor of `359ed69a`, as the Verification note says.

### ② Semver level
